source: Cherry (1953) Some experiments on the recognition of speech, with one and with two ears
finding: Founding dichotic shadowing task: repeat aloud the message in one ear, ignore the other. Listeners shadowed well but could report only physical features of the ignored message (voice gender, speech vs tone), not its content.
numbers: No numbers from the original. Secondary description only (Conway, Cowan and Bunting 2001, opened).
limits: Original not opened (paywalled). Description is from Conway et al. 2001 and the 2024 own-name paper (opened). Cherry also found listeners noticed physical changes but not language changes in the ignored ear.
agent_relevance: Background only: an agent that attends to one stream may be nearly blind to the content of others. Context present is not context read.

source: Broadbent (1958) Perception and Communication
finding: Early-selection filter model: stimuli enter a sensory buffer in parallel, a single-channel filter passes one channel chosen on physical features (voice, location, colour), and only that channel reaches the limited-capacity perceptual system. Unselected input is blocked before identification.
numbers: No numbers: theory book, not opened.
quote: environmental stimulation is filtered out of awareness if it is identified as irrelevant
limits: Not opened. Characterisation from Conway et al. 2001 and Macdonald and Lavie 2008 (both opened).
agent_relevance: Early selection = a hard pre-filter before the model reads anything. Our schema keeps selection in code (G5).

source: Moray (1959) Attention in dichotic listening: affective cues and the influence of instructions
finding: Own-name breakthrough: a participant shadowing one ear sometimes notices their own name in the unattended ear. This was the first major challenge to a strict physical-feature filter.
numbers: 33% of subjects reported hearing their own name in the unattended message (per Conway et al. 2001). Also 33% responded to a command prefixed by their own name (per the 2024 own-name paper).
quote: Moray found that only 33% of subjects reported hearing their own name
limits: Original not opened. Two thirds of people never noticed their name, so the effect is not universal.
agent_relevance: A priority signal (own name, alarm) needs a bypass past the filter. Matters for alert design.

source: Treisman (1960) Contextual cues in selective listening
finding: Attenuation model: the filter does not block unattended input, it turns its volume down. Words with a low recognition threshold (own name, urgent words, contextually expected words) can still break through.
numbers: No numbers read. The ear-switch evidence (shadowers following a sentence that moves to the other ear) is from memory, not verified this session.
limits: Not opened. Described as an early-selection account that allows some processing of the unattended channel (Har-shai Yahav and Zion Golumbic 2021; Macdonald and Lavie 2008, both opened).
agent_relevance: Attenuation is the closest analogue to soft attention weights: low weight, not zero. Weak unattended content can still leak into an answer.

source: Deutsch and Deutsch (1963) Attention: some theoretical considerations
finding: Late-selection model: all input is identified in parallel and automatically; selection happens after identification, by importance, at response or memory. Poor memory of the ignored channel is a memory failure, not a perception failure.
numbers: No numbers: theory paper, not opened.
limits: Not opened. The memory-failure objection is documented in Macdonald and Lavie 2008 (opened).
agent_relevance: Late selection describes a model that reads everything and decides later. That is a plain long-context LLM.

source: Norman (1968) Toward a theory of memory and attention
finding: Pertinence model: all input activates stored representations; selection depends on sensory activation plus pertinence (current task relevance). The most active representation wins.
numbers: No numbers: not opened.
limits: Not opened. Listed as a late-selection account in Macdonald and Lavie 2008 (opened). Detail from memory.
agent_relevance: Pertinence is a task-relevance score added to salience. A ranking step in code can implement it.

source: Treisman and Geffen (1967) Selective attention: perception or response?
finding: Online test of the memory-failure objection: targets in either ear were reported live. Very few unattended-channel targets were reported while most attended-channel ones were. Supports early or attenuated selection without relying on memory.
numbers: Direction only, as stated in Macdonald and Lavie 2008. Exact percentages not read.
limits: Original not opened.
agent_relevance: Low uptake of unselected input is not just forgetting. Logging a stream the agent never attended to will not help.

source: Eriksen and Eriksen (1974) Effects of noise letters upon identification of a target letter in a nonsearch task
finding: Flanker task: response to a central target is slower when flankers map to the opposite response, so irrelevant flankers are identified. Read as support for late selection.
numbers: No numbers read. Cited in Macdonald and Lavie 2008 as support for unattended distractor perception.
limits: Not opened. Eriksen and Hoffman 1972 and Yantis and Johnston 1990 used the same response-competition measure and found no distractor perception outside the attention spotlight (per Macdonald and Lavie 2008): same measure, opposite verdicts.
agent_relevance: Irrelevant-but-similar context competes at the answer stage. Compare GSM-IC distractor effects in LLMs.

source: Macdonald and Lavie (2008) Load induced blindness
finding: Test of perceptual load theory using awareness reports. A task-irrelevant cross was detected far less often under high perceptual load. Working-memory load did not change detection sensitivity (d prime).
numbers: Exp 1, N=16, cross on 12 of 72 trials per block, 100 ms display. Including error trials: detection 37% (d prime 1.31) at high load vs 90% (d prime 3.68) at low load; d prime F(1,14)=11.90, p=.004. Search errors 11% vs 3%.
limits: Single lab, small N, letter-search displays. Snowden and Gray 2025 failed to replicate load effects on distractor interference (a11).
agent_relevance: Supports a hybrid: selection stringency depends on task difficulty. A heavy reasoning step leaves less room for side information.

source: Lavie (1995) Perceptual load as a necessary condition for selective attention
finding: Perceptual load theory: perception is limited in capacity but processes everything automatically until capacity runs out. Low-load displays leave spare capacity that spills to distractors (late-like). High load exhausts capacity (early-like). Resolves early vs late by making selection depend on load.
numbers: Classic result as described in Snowden and Gray 2025: congruent and incongruent RTs differ at low load but are similar at high load (Lavie and Tsal 1994 pattern).
limits: Original not opened. Rivals: dilution account (Tsal and Benoni 2010), salience models (Neokleous et al. 2016), per Snowden and Gray 2025.
agent_relevance: A rule to test: narrower, cleaner context for heavier reasoning steps. Design idea, not evidence.

source: Snowden and Gray (2025) Reduction in distraction due to perceptual load: a failure to replicate
finding: Six experiments failed to find the signature load effect. Central distractors produced strong distraction and congruence effects at both low and high load. Peripheral distractors gave weaker effects, also independent of load. 200 ms displays (Exp 2) and a 2 vs 6 element load contrast (Exp 3) did not rescue it.
numbers: Incongruent minus congruent RT, low load vs high load (ms): Exp1 111 vs 95; Exp2 79 vs 70; Exp3 123 vs 111; Exp4 31 vs 26; Exp5 23 vs 25; Exp6 13 vs 31. Exp1 N=39 (3 removed), Exp2 N=32. Neutral-distractor cost Exp1: 57 vs 60 ms.
quote: Our findings thus do not support the tenants of perceptual load theory
limits: Distractor mostly at centre, unlike the classic peripheral placement. Load still slowed target RTs (Exp1 no-distractor 613 to 791 ms). Dilution and salience accounts also did not fit.
agent_relevance: Do not build design rules on one contested theory. Treat load-dependent filtering as a hypothesis to test.

source: Conway, Cowan and Bunting (2001) The cocktail party phenomenon revisited: the importance of working memory capacity
finding: Low working-memory-span people noticed their own name in the ignored ear far more often than high-span people. Breakthrough reflects weaker inhibition of the ignored channel, not spare capacity.
numbers: N=40 undergraduates (extreme quartiles of operation span, 20 per group). Name noticed by 20% of high-span vs 65% of low-span; Fisher exact p=.005. No one reported a yoked control name. Shadowing errors M=20.88 low-span vs 10.00 high-span, t(32)=2.18, p=.04. Span scores M=24.85 high vs 8.22 low.
quote: subjects who detect their name in the irrelevant message have relatively low working-memory capacities
limits: Retrospective report right after the task. One voice pair, 330-word attended message, name inserted at 4 and 5 min. Small N.
agent_relevance: Better inhibition of side content may matter more than reading more.

source: Wood and Cowan (1995) The cocktail party phenomenon revisited: how frequent are attention shifts to ones own name in an irrelevant auditory channel?
finding: Replicated Moray with better equipment and found the same breakthrough rate.
numbers: 34.6% of subjects reported hearing their own name (per Conway et al. 2001, opened).
limits: Original not opened. Roughly one third in both studies, so the rate is stable across 36 years.
agent_relevance: A stable base rate (about 1 in 3) is a useful calibration for any test of whether an agent notices a side cue.

source: Roer and Cowan (2021), as summarised in Li et al. (2024)
finding: Own name captured attention and caused shadowing errors; unexpected words that deviated from their semantic context were rarely detected and did not affect shadowing. Personal significance beats generic oddness.
numbers: No numbers in the summary. Replications put own-name noticing at "around 30 to 40%" of shadowers.
limits: Original not opened; known only through the 2024 paper (a15).
agent_relevance: Relevance should be computed from the task, not from how surprising a token is.

source: Li, Sanderson and colleagues (2024) Attention capture by own name decreases with speech compression
finding: Own name played during a visual word categorisation task slowed responses by over 100 ms, then habituated across blocks. When the spoken name was time compressed, participants stopped noticing it consciously.
numbers: Exp 1: N=37 (39 enrolled, 2 removed), 22,033 trials; 37 of 37 reported hearing own name. Exp 2 reported hearing own name: 57% compression 24/24; 38% 20/24 (83%); 25% only 4/23 (17%). In the later name-detection block own-name accuracy 100%, median latency 901 ms vs 1085 ms for other names.
quote: participants' word categorization was slower by over 100 ms when their own name was heard
limits: Cantonese names made with text-to-speech. Student sample. Capture vs interference not separated.
agent_relevance: The bypass fails when the input is weakly encoded: high-priority input must also be clear to get through.

source: Har-shai Yahav and Zion Golumbic (2021) Linguistic processing of task-irrelevant speech at a cocktail party
finding: MEG with a hierarchical-frequency design found neural tracking of syntactic structure in task-irrelevant speech, including left inferior frontal cortex. Attended speech was tracked less well when the competitor was natural speech than random syllables. Authors: selective attention does not fully eliminate linguistic processing of competing speech.
numbers: Two experiments, n=29 and n=23. 1 Hz peak Structured vs Non-Structured: p=0.045 (ITPC), left hemisphere p=0.026; source cluster in left inferior frontal cortex p=0.0058; further cluster p=0.002.
quote: Syntactic structure-building processes can be applied to speech that is task-irrelevant and should be ignored
limits: Their intro calls the field "often-conflicting"; some studies find no processing beyond acoustics (Carlyon 2001, Lachter 2004, Ding 2018). Some p values are near .05.
agent_relevance: Graded, not all-or-none, selection fits an agent where unselected context is down-weighted but not removed.

source: Brainstem study (2025) The auditory brainstem response to natural speech is not affected by selective attention
finding: EEG with an eardrum electrode and natural speech: two simultaneous audiobooks, diotic and dichotic. No attention effect in auditory nerve or brainstem; the first effect appears in cortex.
numbers: Bayes factors: wave V size BF0+ shows moderate evidence against an attention effect (3 to 10 band); wave V latency BF01 about 4; CAP measures inconclusive (few subjects with the eardrum electrode).
limits: Intro states earlier studies are split: some report subcortical effects, others do not. First authors and exact N not recorded.
agent_relevance: Even in the brain, filtering is not at the very first stage; "early" means early cortical.

source: Mesgarani and Chang (2012) Selective cortical representation of attended speaker in multi-talker speech perception
finding: Intracranial recordings in human auditory cortex during a cocktail-party task: neural responses reconstruct the attended speaker, not the ignored one.
numbers: Numbers not read (full-text fetch failed). Patient count and details from memory only, unverified.
limits: Not opened. Cited as showing attenuation of unattended speech in Har-shai Yahav and Zion Golumbic 2021 (opened).
agent_relevance: Supports attenuation (strong suppression, not zero) of the unselected stream.

source: Attention-Setting and Human Mental Function (2022 review)
finding: Review notes Kahneman and Treisman (1984) called early and late selection paradigms in Kuhn's sense, each with its own methods. Late-selection methods used simple familiar stimuli and favoured efficient processing. Moray's own-name result added significance-based prioritising.
numbers: No new numbers: conceptual review.
limits: Review only, interpretive.
agent_relevance: Which side wins depends on the task: simple tasks look late-selection, hard ones early. Match test design to the intended task.

source: Shi et al. (2023) Large language models can be easily distracted by irrelevant context
finding: GSM-IC: one irrelevant sentence added to a grade-school math problem. Every prompting method tested lost much accuracy. Few problems were solved consistently across all distractor types.
numbers: code-davinci-002 and text-davinci-003. Of problems solved on the original, no more than 18% solved for all distractor types. Fewer than 30% of base problems consistently solved (macro accuracy). text-davinci-003 base accuracy: COT 80.0, LTM 81.0. Role-overlap distractors drove macro accuracy to 0 on problems with more than 2 steps (text-davinci-003).
limits: GPT-3 family only, 2023. Newer models not measured here. Arithmetic only.
agent_relevance: LLMs behave like a late-selection system: irrelevant text enters computation. Strip irrelevant context before solving (G5, code selects).

source: Shi et al. (2023) mitigations
finding: Three fixes: self-consistency with 20 samples raised micro accuracy by more than 11 points; exemplars containing distractors helped; an instruction to ignore irrelevant information helped. Best macro accuracy anywhere was only 45%.
numbers: Self-consistency, 20 samples: micro +11 points overall, +35.5 on zero-shot COT; correct answer present in the 20 samples for 99.7% of problems (COT, LTM), 96.5% for 0-COT. Best macro accuracy 45%.
quote: adding to the prompt an instruction that tells the language model to ignore the irrelevant information
limits: High recall but low consistency: models can produce the answer but get pulled off it. Samples are not independent (our G4).
agent_relevance: An ignore instruction helps somewhat; code-level removal should be stronger.

source: Weston and Sukhbaatar (2023) System 2 Attention
finding: S2A is an LLM-level early selection: first regenerate the context keeping only relevant parts, then answer from the cleaned text. Improved factual QA with opinions in the prompt, GSM-IC math and long-form objectivity.
numbers: LLaMA-2-70B-chat. Factual QA with opinionated prompts: baseline 62.8%, oracle 82.0%, S2A 80.3%. GSM-IC: S2A about +12 points for random distractors and +10 for in-topic (abstract: 51.7% to 61.3%). Long-form objectivity +57.4% (abstract).
quote: S2A regenerates the input context to only include the relevant portions
limits: Two model calls (extra cost). One model.
agent_relevance: Closest match to our schema: a separate pre-filter pass. Test as an operator with code checking what was dropped.

source: Weston and Sukhbaatar (2023) S2A ablations: hard vs soft attention
finding: Keeping the original context visible next to the cleaned one hurt. A debias instruction alone helped less than S2A and still showed sycophancy. Authors conclude attention must be hard, not soft.
numbers: S2A 80.3% vs S2A-KeepOrig 74.5% vs baseline plus debias instruction 71.7% vs baseline 62.8%. Instructed prompting: Suggest Correct 92% (above oracle), Suggest Incorrect 38% vs oracle 82%. On GSM-IC instructed prompting gave no consistent gain.
quote: attention must be hard (sharp) not soft when it comes to avoiding irrelevant or spurious correlations
limits: One model and prompt design. "Must be hard" is the authors' interpretation.
agent_relevance: Strongest LLM case for early selection: remove, do not just down-weight. Matches our rule that the program decides what the model sees.

source: Liu et al. (2023) Lost in the middle: how language models use long contexts
finding: Multi-document QA and key-value retrieval: accuracy is highest when the relevant document is first or last and drops in the middle (U-shaped). Linked by the authors to the human serial-position effect.
numbers: 10, 20 and 30 documents. GPT-3.5-Turbo worst-case drop more than 20 points; with 20 and 30 documents middle-position accuracy fell below closed-book 56.1%. LLaMA-2 13B base: 20-point best-worst gap; 13B fine-tuned 10-point; 70B similar trend.
quote: performance can degrade significantly when changing the position of relevant information
limits: 2023 models (0613 versions). Later models not measured here.
agent_relevance: Selection in an LLM is position-driven, not task-driven. Put critical items at the edges and rank in code.

source: Leviathan, Kalman and Matias (2025) Selective attention improves transformer
finding: A parameter-free change lets a token reduce attention to earlier tokens that are no longer needed (reduce only, never boost). Improves language modelling and cuts memory: trained-in attenuation of unneeded context.
numbers: On C4, equal to standard transformers with 2x more attention heads and parameters. Attention-module memory 16x, 25x, 47x lower at context sizes 512, 1024, 2048 for the same validation perplexity.
quote: Unneeded elements in the attention's context degrade performance.
limits: Needs training; not available to a frozen-model scaffold. Perplexity and C4 only.
agent_relevance: Learned attenuation helps quality. A scaffold can only approximate it by pruning context.

source: Gap check by this agent: LLM papers vs classic theories
finding: I found no LLM study that directly tests dichotic shadowing or own-name breakthrough. The four LLM papers I opened use the human theories at most as metaphor (System 1 and 2, serial position). None mention Broadbent, Treisman, cocktail party or attenuation.
numbers: Full-text grep of Shi, Weston, Liu and Leviathan for Treisman, Broadbent, cocktail, attenuat: zero hits.
limits: WebSearch budget was used up and arXiv, Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex APIs were rate-limited, so absence is not proven. Spoken-language models may have such tests.
agent_relevance: Open slot for our own test: place a decoy stream beside the task and add a name-like high-salience probe; measure leak.
